source.title: An evaluation of circuit evaluation metrics

page_placements.theme: Faithfulness and overlap do not uniquely establish mechanism

record.file_problem: None; the full post is present.
record.tranche_reason: It argues that the formal faithfulness, completeness, and minimality metrics cited in V1 can give counterintuitive results, using constructed toy examples. It does not evaluate the GPT-2 small IOI circuit itself.
record.gate_note: No GPT-2 small IOI performance, ablation, or circuit-head role is measured. The post's toy examples apply the circuit metrics, so their results are recorded with versions ["none"]. The mention that backup heads occur naturally in transformers cites the IOI paper and is not a result from this study. The stated constant-subcircuit outputs and F(C) scores are assumptions in the examples.
record.test_reason: The post gives a specific argument that the IOI paper's faithfulness, completeness and minimality formalisations can mislabel circuits. It supports this only with toy networks whose F(C) values are stipulated. It measures no GPT-2 small circuit, ablation, or IOI rate, so it bears on how V1's criteria should be read, not on whether the circuit meets them. No verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors argue that the IOI paper's formalisations of faithfulness, completeness and minimality allow counterintuitive outcomes. Completeness subsumes faithfulness and ignores added components, and minimality is node-level and granularity-dependent. They plan revised or complementary metrics and a study of ablation types.
record.recipe_differences: This is a conceptual critique of circuit evaluation metrics with constructed toy examples, not an empirical reproduction of the original GPT-2 IOI circuit analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The post says ablation choice can affect faithfulness in principle and demonstrates that minimality results can change with the granularity of the abstract model. It does not measure these effects on IOI.

fits_no_version.finding: In the toy backup-head network, completeness counts only the circuit containing both B_1 and B_2 as complete.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the IOI completeness formalisation, a circuit must include all backup components to count as complete.

fits_no_version.finding: In the toy constant-subcircuit network, {A,-1,+1} and {A} are both faithful, complete and minimal. {A,-1} is minimal yet incomplete, and becomes complete when -1 is removed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Node-level minimality and knockout-based completeness can give counterintuitive classifications, including minimal circuits that have smaller, equally good circuits.

record.problems: The examples are constructed toy scenarios, and the F(C) values are stipulated rather than measured on a model. The post does not test whether its metric critiques alter the evaluation of the GPT-2 small IOI circuit.
record.rows_left_out: Other circuit entries in the Backup heads and Constant sub-circuit tables, along with the alternative-granularity examples, are omitted; they are further entries in the same constructed demonstrations and do not test the GPT-2 IOI circuit.

untested.parts: Whether the 26-head, 7-class GPT-2 small circuit meets the criteria. The post critiques the definitions only.
No name-mover ablation or self-repair measured. The backup-head case is a stipulated toy.
No other models, sizes, checkpoints or task reuse.
No alternative discovery methods, ablations or metrics compared on IOI.
Ablation dependence (zero vs resample on constant subcircuits) and granularity dependence of minimality are argued in principle only. Nothing is measured on IOI.
No prompt variants, name orders, templates or name counts.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are toy constructions with stipulated F(C) values, so versions ['none'] is right. The rows are correctly read from the appendix tables. The text has internal slips. The completeness section cites {A,+1} where the table discussion centres on {A,-1}. The Σ-granularity paragraph says the full circuit 'is minimal', although its reasoning implies non-minimal. The post is a LessWrong MATS write-up with no empirical IOI results. If V5 is later broadened to include in-principle arguments about metric formalisation, this post would be relevant discussion, but it remains untested evidence.

versions.untested_parts: The GPT-2 small IOI circuit, its 26 heads and 7 classes, and whether that circuit meets the stated criteria were not tested.
No GPT-2 small name-mover ablation or self-repair was tested; the backup-head example is a constructed toy scenario.
No other models, sizes, checkpoints, or task reuse were tested.
No alternative circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics were compared on IOI.
The post notes that ablation choice can affect faithfulness in principle, but does not test IOI performance across ablations, metrics, or prompt distributions.
No IOI prompt variants, name orders, templates, or numbers of names were tested.
